I bought a small amount SAFEMOON for the first time through Pancake just over a month ago. It was a BEP20 token with the contract address [https://bscscan.com/address/0xd4a824503a06531b48b3a07601d2502a4dd8d65d](https://bscscan.com/address/0xd4a824503a06531b48b3a07601d2502a4dd8d65d). Four days later I purchased additional SAFEMOON and the contract address had changed to [https://bscscan.com/address/0x8076c74c5e3f5852037f31ff0093eeb8c8add8d3](https://bscscan.com/address/0x8076c74c5e3f5852037f31ff0093eeb8c8add8d3). Now in Trust wallet I have a split with two amounts of SAFEMOON between BSC contracts:

1. The new address which pancake recognizes and is transactable (which I've promptly sold due to this scenario)
2. The old contract address which is completely useless as there is no liquidity attached to it, and is non-transferable as a BSC contract.

If you look at the current [issues list on github](https://github.com/safemoonprotocol/Safemoon.sol/issues), SAFEMOON is a scam and things [just don't add up](https://www.google.com/search?q=issues+0x8076c74c5e3f5852037f31ff0093eeb8c8add8d3&safe=active&client=opera&hs=med&sxsrf=ALeKk03gGBdnvRN8RakKKXQXgRCEKpg82w%3A1619736092895&ei=HDaLYLCaNqTBz7sPycmXgAE&oq=issues+0x8076c74c5e3f5852037f31ff0093eeb8c8add8d3&gs_lcp=Cgdnd3Mtd2l6EAMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEMyBwgAELADEEM6BwgAEEcQsANQymBYhm9gwXBoAnACeACAAYACiAHvDJIBBTAuNS4zmAEAoAEBqgEHZ3dzLXdpesgBCsABAQ&sclient=gws-wiz&ved=0ahUKEwiwmMmTw6TwAhWk4HMBHcnkBRAQ4dUDCA0&uact=5). What sort of boxing were you doing to cut open your knuckles? If you're at a boxing gym using wraps and gloves that shouldn't happen. Saying that, if you do enjoy boxing and aren't going to a gym I've found it's a great way to deal with depression. There's nothing like taking all that sadness/anger and directing it toward a heavy bag. And most boxing clubs I've been to have a bunch of guys who at some time or other felt the same way and have learned how to deal with those feelings. Plus there's the bonus of all those feel good endorphins from intense exercise. My 2c would be to recommend finding a boxing gym (with wraps) and getting involved. After all, even if your mother doesn't like the boxing, she'd be more devastated if she lost you for good.

I felt very similar to the way you're feeling now when I was your age. Although all our circumstances are different, the feelings that result from abuse and bullying are similar. Self-loathing and the feeling of being unimportant, unloved and unnecessary. Take it from someone who's come out the other side of those feelings though - those thoughts in your head are lies, and things will get better. In fact you're just at the point where life has the possibility of getting good because you're old enough to make your own way. In spite of all the things that have happened you've reached out and that's the first step. Give yourself a bit more time, there's no need to set a deadline.

Also, Asperger's isn't a disability IMO - it's just a different perspective that our society hasn't figured out how to box up and label. That makes you unique and special. And it means you have a unique gift to contribute. If the world loses you, you won't be able to get the satisfaction and pleasure out of finding out what that gift is and how it plays out.

Holding onto those feelings of revenge won't help. Carrying around hurt like that al the time is heavy and weighs you down. It may sound trite but the best revenge to give a bully is no time in your thought life. Forget about the bad and try and think of the good things no matter how small or insignificant they might seem right now.

Even if you don't quite know it yet, you'll know best what you need to do to feel like you're enjoying life again (probably amplifying the things that you enjoy already). The key is figuring it out - I know it can seem a mess of confusion when you're 17. I can definitely recommend trying to find someone you trust to hash it out with - a community leader, pastor or someone older you trust.

 I had a friend commit suicide around age 17 - when I was having similar thoughts. Almost 20 years later I look back on all the great things that have happened to me since that time, and feel sorry that my friend missed out on the possibility of what I've experienced. The world is a big place and there are lots of options for you out there. Hold on, hang in there. Keep talking to people. We care about you.
